segmenti.tekst: [Arabic recitation]

…wa ala alihi wa sahbihi ajma'in. Praise belongs to the One, Exalted Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala (glorified and exalted is He), Lord of all the worlds. Praise be to Him for gathering us here this evening to study His religion, to worship Him alone, and to follow His Messenger Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him). May Allah's pleasure be upon the companions of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and upon all those who follow their path.
Amin, ya Rabb al-alamin. In the last lecture, dear brothers, we spoke about the importance of worshipping Allah alone, the One, the Only.
And we said that every messenger who was sent called first to belief, that is, to the worship of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the One, the Only. And that was their first duty, or their first task.

As Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an: “وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِي إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدُونِ” – “And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity worthy of worship except Me,” says Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, “so worship Me.”

So worship Me. So the main task of every messenger was to call to the worship of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the One, the Only. We also mentioned the hadith of the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, which speaks about the right of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, over His servants.

So Allah has this right over us: that we worship Him and do not commit shirk with Him, that we do not ascribe partners to Him. And our right with our Lord is that He does not punish the one who says “La ilaha illallah”, seeking His pleasure, seeking to see His Face in Jannah (Paradise).

We also mentioned here that worship is not only that a person falls into prostration before Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. That is not the only act of worship. There are many acts of worship that a person must not perform for, or direct to, anyone other than Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

Among those acts of worship, dear brothers, is “al-isti'adhah”, or seeking protection. We can say that the technical meaning of “al-isti'adhah” is turning to Allah, relying on Him and firmly resorting to Him, seeking refuge and protection with Him from all evils and harms that can befall a person.
Why do we mention “al-isti'adhah”? Because this term, “al-isti'adhah”, is mentioned in the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

So it is not permissible, that is, it is not permissible to seek protection from evil, from Satan or from other things, except with Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an: “O Messenger, O Muhammad, if Satan incites you to some evil, or casts doubt into your chest, or anger, seek protection” – with whom? With Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.
Not with some saint, nor with some idol and so on, but with whom? With Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. “Innahu sami'un alim” – indeed, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

Also, a verse that proves that this is worship and that it must not be done for, or directed to, anyone other than Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, is the verse in which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: “Wa qul Rabbi a'udhu bika min hamazat ash-shayatin, wa a'udhu bika Rabbi an yahdurun.” And say, O Muhammad: I seek protection with Allah from the incitements of the devils, from his incitements, from his whisperings. “Wa a'udhu bika… an yahdurun” –

and I seek protection with You, my Lord, from their presence. How beautiful these verses are, for a person to learn them so that he may seek protection from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Also the surahs, dear brothers, that we all know, which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sent to the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, as a cure.

You all know that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was afflicted by magic. You all know that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was afflicted by magic. And no trial passed him by. And all of this so that we, as his ummah, would benefit from it.

So that we, as his ummah, would benefit from it. He was bewitched by a Jew named Labid, together with his daughters. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sent both surahs: “Qul a'udhu bi Rabb al-falaq” and “Qul a'udhu bi Rabb an-nas”. And what does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say in Surah Al-Falaq: “Qul” – say, O Muhammad – “a'udhu bi Rabb al-falaq” – I seek protection with the Lord of the daybreak – “min sharri ma khalaq” – from the evil, from the harm
of what He has created – “wa min sharri ghasiqin idha waqab” – and from the evil, or harm, of the night when it spreads its darkness. And you know, you see how precise it is here – the night.
Most evil happens precisely at night, that is, when it is night. And truly, when night falls, that is when evil spreads. Because people simply cannot see each other, they hide,

and then they do all kinds of evil. So Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, here tells the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, to seek protection with Him from every evil. “Wa min sharri ghasiqin idha waqab,
wa min sharri an-naffathati fil-'uqad” – and I seek protection with You, Lord, from those sorceresses who blow on knots. And we… no, we today…

That is, wallahi, today this has been cleaned up quite a bit. In the past, you know, these old folks – someone would go and have lead poured for him against fright. Lead is poured for him against fright, or he is treated by a woman who, by Allah, cannot pronounce a single letter properly,

but instead she utters some words that cannot even be understood. And then she asks for, I don't know, a picture, a piece of clothing and so on. And these are all signs that this person is a sorcerer,

and that she works with jinn, with devils. So Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, through His Messenger, taught us here how to protect ourselves from these evils. “Wa min sharri an-naffathati fil-'uqad, wa min sharri hasidin idha hasad” –

and from the evil, the harm of the envier – but not every envier: the one who envies. There are people who envy but do not wish harm; their envy does not pass on to others. And there is the envier who envies and wants to destroy the one he envies.

How comprehensively Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, covered everything with this surah, how Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sent this surah as a cure for mankind through the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. And I simply cannot understand people, dear brothers: a man comes from the Sandžak, from Bosnia, to Medina, and what does he do?

He commits shirk, disbelief, at the grave of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, seeking protection from the Prophet, or asking the dead, our Prophet, to intercede for him. That is unbelievable. If the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, could have cured himself,

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, would not have sent him these surahs; rather, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, would have cured himself. But no. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, like us, cannot bring himself any benefit or ward off harm,

except as much as Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has decreed for him, and for us as well. Also, Surah An-Nas – also a cure. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says, addressing the Prophet and his ummah as well: “Qul a'udhu bi Rabb an-nas” –

say, O Muhammad: I seek protection with the Lord of mankind – “Malik an-nas” – the King of mankind – “Ilah an-nas” – their God – “min sharri al-waswas al-khannas” – from the evil, the harm of Satan, who, when Allah's name is mentioned, quickly flees and does not stay.
So we see here, then, a proof that when Allah's name is mentioned, Satan quickly, quickly flees. “Alladhi yuwaswisu fi suduri an-nas” – who casts doubt into the chests of people,

doubt, disbelief and so on. “Min al-jinnati wan-nas” – from among the jinn and mankind. Also, here we have proof that there are devils from among humans and devils from among the jinn. So someone will ask: how is there evil, or how does the evil that happens occur in the month of Ramadan, when the devils are chained?

Did the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, not inform us that the devils are chained in the month of Ramadan? He did. But there remain these devils from among humans. Devils from among humans. Devils from among humans who walk about.

When the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was asked: “Are there devils from among humans?”, the Prophet said: “There are. There are.” So a person should recite these two surahs as a cure and seek protection only from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. It is narrated in a hadith reported by Abdullah ibn Abbas, and recorded by Bukhari, that the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, taught them a supplication; he said: “He taught us this supplication as he taught us Surah Al-Baqarah.”

Which supplication is that, dear brothers? It is the supplication recited at the end of every prayer. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: “Qulu” – say – “Allahumma inna na'udhu bika min 'adhabi jahannam.”

O my Allah, I seek protection with You from the punishment of Jahannam (Hellfire), from the punishment of Jahannam. From the punishment of Jahannam. As you see, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, first says that we should seek protection from the Fire of Jahannam.

With whom should we seek protection? With Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. We must not seek protection from the Fire of Jahannam with anyone else. You see, believe me, people who seek protection from the Fire of Jahannam with some saint, with some jinn, with some fifth or ninth one,

forget Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. They forget, they forget Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. And the first thing a person should seek protection from is Jahannam. And that is a quality of people of understanding, as Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in the Qur'an: “الَّذِينَ يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَى جُنُوبِهِمْ” –

those, He says, who remember Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, standing and sitting, and sitting and lying on their sides – “وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ” [unclear] “رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا بَاطِلًا” [unclear] “رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا بَاطِلًا سُبْحَانَكَ” [unclear] “فَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ” –

we seek protection with You from the Fire of Jahannam. The second thing the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, mentions, he says: we seek protection with You from the trial, or the punishment of the grave, or the torment of the grave. The torment of the grave is one of the greatest trials for a person, one of the greatest trials for a person. When Munkar and Nakir come and question the person, after his family

and his friends have moved away from the graveyard – Munkar and Nakir come and ask him three things. The first thing is: “Who was your Lord? Whom did you worship in this world?” The second thing is: “What was your religion?”

The third thing is: “Who was your messenger?” You know, sometimes we think: we will answer that easily. And sometimes we think: we will answer that easily. If you asked anyone of us here now, he would certainly answer,

that is, it would be the correct answer. But no: in the grave a person will not answer the way he would answer in this world, but according to his deeds and his belief. So, according to how we acted, that is how we will answer in the grave.

So that is one of the greatest trials for a person. And a person should seek protection. See how the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, who was the best of creation, sought protection from the torment of the grave.

So what should we do then, dear brothers? A person should learn this. And he says: the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, taught them these things as he taught them Surah Al-Baqarah. We know that Surah Al-Baqarah is the largest surah in the Qur'an, and that in Surah Al-Baqarah is the best verse, the most magnificent verse, Ayat al-Kursi.

Or, as we call it, the “Te'svih-dova”. Also, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: “وَنَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ” – and he said: learn to seek protection with Allah from the fitnah, or trial, of the Dajjal.

We all know who the Dajjal is. The Dajjal is the first sign, a major sign among the signs of the Day of Judgment. The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said that it is the greatest trial for mankind, from Adam to the end of the world.

That is the greatest trial, this worldly trial. So the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, sought protection from the Dajjal, who will cover truth with falsehood, who will present himself as a deity, whom the Jews will follow, and, of course, most of his followers will be women,

as is mentioned in the narrations. And finally the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: “وَنَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَحْيَا وَالْمَمَاتِ” – and he said: I seek refuge, or I seek protection with You, my Lord, from the trials of life and death.
What does this mean, dear brothers? It means that a person should seek protection from the trials that will strike him in life. And you know, during a person's life various trials, well, strike him.

There are trials that a person faces, and those are sins. For some people sins are a trial. Or is it not so? When a beautiful woman comes to him, when alcohol comes to him and so on – all of that is a trial.

So a person should… For some, money is a trial; for some, something else is a trial. So it is up to a person to seek protection from these things. With whom? With Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Also, also he says: the trial, and that we seek protection from the trial, the trial of death.

What does this mean, dear brothers? That we seek protection from the trial when the angel comes, when the angel of death comes. And that is a great trial, the greatest trial, when the angel of death comes: will a person in those moments say “La ilaha illallah” and pass away as a believer, or will he pass away as a disbeliever?

You know that there will come a time near the end of this world when a person will go to sleep as a believer and wake up as a disbeliever. Believe me, dear brothers, I have seen it, I have seen such people, who learned, dear brothers, two juz' of the Qur'an, and then all of a sudden – gone.

He disbelieves in Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, in His existence, in everything. That is why it is very important for a person to learn this supplication, to know what to seek protection from. Also, among the acts of worship, among the acts of worship, dear brothers, is seeking, seeking help, seeking help.

Here we are not talking, dear brothers, about the help that each of us seeks from his Muslim brother who is able to help him; rather, here we are talking about something that no one can obtain for a person except Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Can anyone extend our life except Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala? A person cannot, if he asks that of someone else. Or protect him from the Fire of Jahannam – only Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, can do that. And the proof, the proof that this is worship is the verse we recite every day, there is no rak'ah in which we do not recite it: “Iyyaka na'budu” –

You alone we worship, or we worship no one other than You – “wa iyyaka nasta'in” – and from You alone we seek help. If Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, had not wanted us to seek help from Him, He would not have revealed these verses to us. And in Arabic this is called “al-hasr”, that is, restriction: that we ask, ask, ask only of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. So this first sentence, “iyyaka na'budu”, is a renunciation of false deities; “wa iyyaka nasta'in” – and from You we seek help – is a renunciation

of one's own power, one's own strength, and a surrender of oneself to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Also, a hadith that indicates that this is worship, seeking help from Allah, is the hadith – a very beautiful hadith, which we should teach our children – narrated by Abdullah ibn Abbas.

He said: “I was behind the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam,” that is, I was walking behind the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. Ibn Abbas was small, quite young. And today, when we want to tell our children something, we say: “Never mind, he's little.” We say: “Never mind, he's still little, he won't understand it.”

And then the time comes, when he grows up, that he really won't understand, he doesn't want to understand. That is why, dear brothers, children are brought up from an early age. So we see, this is an example, the example of the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. There is no more beautiful example than the example of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. What does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say to him?

He said: “O boy,” he said, “I will teach you some words.” The first thing the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, taught him, he said: “Ihfazillaha yahfazka” – guard Allah, and Allah will guard you.

What does it mean, dear brothers? The Prophet says, that is, the scholars say: this means guard the limits set by Allah, hold to what Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has commanded you and keep away from what He has forbidden you – and He will guard you.

“Guard Allah, and you will find Him beside you,” that is, you will find Him as a helper in every situation. If you guard His limits and do not transgress His limits, He will help you in every situation.

This is a promise of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. This is a promise of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, through His Messenger. And he does not speak, that is, the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, does not speak of his own inclination,

rather it is revelation revealed to him from his Lord. What does the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say next? He says: “If you ask for something, ask of Allah.” Why? Because Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala,

is the best Giver and the best One to ask of. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will not turn back empty the hands of a believer who supplicates to Him. And if He does not give it to him in this world – and Allah knows why He does not give him a certain thing – He will surely give it to him in the Hereafter.

He says further: “وَإِذَا اسْتَعَنْتَ فَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ” – and he says: when you seek help, seek it only from Allah. Why? The explanation comes after that; he says: “Wa'lam anna al-ummata law ijtama'at 'ala an yanfa'uka bi shay'in lam yanfa'uka illa bi shay'in qad katabahullahu lak” – and know, and know, that if the whole world gathered together to bring you some benefit,

they could not bring it to you except as much as Allah has decreed for you. The proof, dear brothers: that sister of ours who passed away a few… Did we not all gather to help her in her illness, to make it easier for her, so that she could go for an operation?
But that was it, Allah had not decreed it for her. It was in vain that we gathered and collected money.

Simply, Allah had not decreed it. And so, he says further: “Wa in ijtama'u 'ala an yadurruka bi shay'in lam yadurruka illa bi shay'in qad katabahullahu 'alayk.” And he says: if they all gathered together to do you some harm,
he says, they could not do it to you except as much as Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has decreed it. It is not possible. Allah has decreed it, written it.
“The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.” That is, Allah wrote the destiny of man 50,000 years before He created the heavens and the Earth.

So a person does not have to, and must not, fear for the future. Believe me, there are people who are afraid; they say: “What will I do when I get old? Will I be left alone? Will my children abandon me?” First, who promises us that we will live to old age? Second, who tells us, or why do we fear, that our children will abandon us, or our wife, or that we will be left to live alone and so on?

A person should not think about that. That is why all of this, all of this – so that a person relies on Allah and seeks help from Allah and protection from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Also, dear brothers, one of the beautiful acts of worship is offering the qurban (sacrifice).

Offering the qurban to Allah alone, subhanahu wa ta'ala. It is one of the most beautiful acts of worship, it is one of the most beautiful acts of worship. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says, addressing His Messenger – since, you know, the polytheists offered sacrifices, or offerings, to their idols,

to their idols, and bowed down to them – so Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, tells His Messenger to convey to the Quraysh, the polytheists, these words: “Qul” – say, O Muhammad – “inna salati” – indeed my prayer – “wa nusuki” – and my sacrifice, my offering – “wa mahyaya” – and my life – “wa mamati” – and my death – “lillahi Rabb al-alamin” – belong only to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. “La sharika lah” –

He has no partner. “Wa bi dhalika umirtu” – and this I have been commanded – “wa ana awwalu al-muslimin” – and I am the first Muslim of this ummah, says the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, the first Muslim of this ummah. We see here, here, how Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentioned the slaughtering of the sacrifice after the prayer. And that is proof of how great and beautiful an act of worship it is. And believe me, dear brothers, one of the most beautiful moments of the year for me is when, during Eid al-

Adha, I wish to offer a sacrifice to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, together with my family. That is the most beautiful moment. So a person must not slaughter a sacrifice, a qurban, for anyone other than Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. If he does so, then he is a polytheist, a disbeliever – it's over for him, over, over, it's over for him. Dear brothers, it is also very important, when a person slaughters a qurban, or not only a qurban, anything else – that is, if a person slaughters, I don't know,

a cow, to feed his family, then he must mention Allah's name, so that it is for the sake of Allah. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say? He says: “Do not eat of that which has been slaughtered and over which Allah's name has not been mentioned – wa innahu la fisq” – indeed, that is disobedience. That is disobedience to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. That is why we also recite the surah “Inna a'taynaka al-Kawthar” – indeed, We have given you the river of Kawthar

in Jannah – “fa salli li Rabbika wanhar” – so pray to your Lord, that is, perform the prayer for Him, and slaughter the sacrifice, that is, offer a sacrifice to Him. We see here too that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentioned the offering of sacrifice, that is, the qurban, after the prayer. How beautiful, how very, very beautiful an act of worship it is! It is narrated from Abu Tufayl – and Abu Tufayl was a companion who spent much time with Ali, that is, he learned from Ali, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu (may Allah be pleased with him) – that this Abu Tufayl once asked Ali, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu: “Ali, has Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, given you, or you and his family,

some knowledge apart from other people? Do you know something that other people do not know, that the other companions do not know?” Why this question, dear brothers? You know that the Shi'a, the Rafidah – some go so far as to worship Ali, and they think that the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, gave Ali some knowledge that he did not give to the other companions,

that is, that the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, told him something that he did not tell the other companions. So Ali, radiyallahu anhu, refutes these claims; he said: “No, except one thing, except one thing.” And, it is said, he took out of the sheath of his sword a paper on which was written: “Allah has cursed the one who slaughters, or offers a sacrifice, to anyone other than Allah.”

Why does Ali say this? Because he heard the hadith from the Prophet. Ali was one of the most learned companions, one of the most learned, because he was young when the revelation came to the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, so he memorized quickly.

He memorized quickly, both hadiths and everything. And then he says: “Allah has cursed,” he says, “the one who slaughters something in someone else's name, and not in Allah's, in Allah's name.” So offering the qurban is worship, dear brothers. And the last thing that we will, in sha Allah, mention today is the vow. The vow. The vow, or “nadhr” in Islam, is an act of obedience that a person makes obligatory

upon himself. That is, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, did not make it obligatory for him; rather, the person made it obligatory upon himself. For example, a person says: “I vow: if Allah cures this child of mine, I will fast every day.”
He must fast. That is: “I vow.” And it is not permissible for a person to make a vow to anyone other than Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.
You cannot say: “I vow: if this saint, or that one in the grave, cures my child, I will [unclear].” You cannot. That is, you must say: this belongs only to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

When a person makes a vow to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, he must fulfil it. And perhaps all of us have at some time made some vow to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, praises those people in the Qur'an; He says: “Yufuna bin-nadhr” – He says: they fulfil the vow – “wa yakhafuna yawman kana sharruhu mustatira” – and such people, He says, fear a day whose… a day when its evil, or the evil of that day, or the harm of that day, will be widespread, that is, the Day of Judgment, the horrors of the Day of Judgment. So these people fear the horrors of the Day, the Day of Judgment, and fulfil their vows.

Aisha, radiyallahu ta'ala anha (may Allah be pleased with her), narrates; she said: “Man nadhara an yuti'allaha falyuti'hu” – he said: whoever vows to obey Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala – like the example we briefly mentioned, mentioned a little earlier – he said: “let him follow Him, let him obey Him”; and, he said, “whoever vows to disobey Him, or to sin against Him, cannot do that.”

So if a person vows to disobey Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, he must not fulfil it. For example: a person vows that he will commit some sin: “I will commit such and such a sin if such and such happens to me, I vow to Allah.” It cannot be like that. That is invalid.

That is an invalid vow, and a person should keep away from it. Today, dear brothers, we have finished with one very important… and that is the chapter that speaks about the importance of worship and of worshipping Allah alone, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

In sha Allah, next week we continue, and that will also be the last lecture before the month of Ramadan. In the month of Ramadan we have our activities, where we will have a short lecture before every fajr prayer, and after Ramadan, in sha Allah, we continue with this beautiful book that speaks about the foundations of the religion.

I understand that sometimes perhaps a person… these things, especially when fiqh matters come up, or matters related to wudu (ablution), prayer and so on, perhaps someone will find them a bit boring, because most people, that is, most of us, know these things. But these things are very important, so that a person consolidates them a little better, so that tomorrow he can teach his family.

This, dear brothers, that you learn here, or what you hear here, a person should remember, and then tomorrow warn someone from his family or someone among his close ones. Because all of us, dear brothers, are callers to Allah's religion. How many of us are here? A handful, as our people would say, a handful of souls.

A handful of souls. How many people are outside right now who are not interested in religion, nor in the mosque, nor in anything at all. That is why, dear brothers, we are the ones who need, who need to teach people these things when we go out.

When we go out, to present this to people in the most beautiful light. And all of us, all of us are callers, and all of us are witnesses that I have conveyed this to you, so you too convey it to others. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among His sincere, good servants. I ask Him, the Exalted, to protect us from the Fire of Jahannam. I ask Him, the Exalted, that we worship Him alone. Amin, ya Rabb al-alamin.
